title: Nārada Muni
summary: The travelling sage whose songs and counsel turn hearts toward devotion and who guides Dhruva, Prahlāda and Vyāsa.
body:
Nārada moves between worlds as a messenger and teacher. His counsel reaches Dhruva in the forest, Prahlāda in a demon's court and Vyāsa after years of gathering Vedic knowledge. In each case he turns the listener toward devotion rather than status.

The entry keeps these connections visible so the figure can be found from more than one story.

title: Prahlāda Mahārāja
summary: A young prince whose steady devotion survives his father's cruelty and becomes an example for others.
body:
Prahlāda is a child devotee whose faith holds firm while his father Hiraṇyakaśipu tries to destroy him. The narrative places surrender above birth and power, and it shows devotion surviving fear, exile and violence.

This entry gathers the main relationships around that story.

title: Dhruva Mahārāja
summary: A prince who leaves home after a slight, performs severe austerity, and is granted a lasting place in the cosmos.
body:
Dhruva leaves home after a wound to his pride and takes to austerity in the forest. His determination becomes devotion, and the narratives grant him a fixed and lasting place in the cosmos.

The description preserves both the early disappointment and the later fulfilment.

title: Ambarīṣa Mahārāja
summary: A righteous king whose simple, steady surrender humbles a proud sage and protects his people.
body:
Ambarīṣa rules the earth but keeps his mind fixed on the Lord. When Durvāsā Muni tests him, the king's steady surrender protects him and humbles the proud sage.

This entry records the balance of kingship and devotion that defines him.

title: Vyāsadeva
summary: The compiler who gathers the ancient Vedic knowledge into lasting forms and teaches the path of devotion to his son.
body:
Vyāsadeva gathers the ancient Vedic knowledge into lasting forms and teaches it to his son Śukadeva. Even after this vast work he feels unsatisfied until he turns to the Lord's pastimes and the path of devotion.

The entry keeps both his role as compiler and his inner turning point.

title: Śukadeva Gosvāmī
summary: A detached sage who narrates the Lord's pastimes to a dying king and awakens faith in his final hours.
body:
Śukadeva is a renounced sage whose detachment is matched by compassion for a dying king. He narrates the Lord's pastimes to Parīkṣit in the king's final days and awakens faith at the edge of death.

This description preserves the setting and the listener.

title: Parīkṣit Mahārāja
summary: An emperor who accepts a curse, renounces his throne, and spends his last seven days hearing the Lord's pastimes.
body:
Parīkṣit is an emperor who accepts a curse, leaves his throne and spends seven days hearing the Lord's pastimes on the bank of the Gaṅgā. His final question becomes the occasion for a full account of devotion.

The entry marks his transition from ruler to seeker.

title: Arjuna
summary: The Pāṇḍava archer who receives Kṛṣṇa's counsel on the battlefield after his resolve fails.
body:
Arjuna is a Pāṇḍava archer and Kṛṣṇa's close companion. On the battlefield he is overcome by grief at the sight of relatives and teachers in the opposing army, and Kṛṣṇa answers with a teaching about duty, knowledge and devotion.

This description keeps both the warrior and the hearer in view.

title: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu
summary: The Vaiṣṇava saint whose life and teaching inspire the Vraja Gosvāmīs and the Gauḍīya path.
body:
Caitanya Mahāprabhu is the centre of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava path followed in Vraja. His life in Navadvīpa, His renunciation and His years in Jagannātha Purī shaped the Gosvāmīs who came after Him.

The entry gathers the main lines of that influence without reducing Him to a single role.

relations.role: Recipient of later association and blessings
Relished his Gīta Govinda in Jagannātha Purī

title: Madhva
summary: The early Vedānta teacher who stands at the beginning of the lineage followed in Vraja.
body:
Madhva stands at the beginning of the lineage honoured by the Vraja Gosvāmīs. His teaching on the supremacy of the Lord gives later teachers a framework for devotion and renunciation.

This entry preserves his place as the first named link in that line.

title: Mādhavendra Purī
summary: A saintly renunciate in the line between Madhva and Īśvara Purī, remembered for tender devotion.
body:
Mādhavendra Purī is a saintly renunciate in the line between Madhva and Īśvara Purī. He is remembered for a tender devotion that softened the heart of even a proud king.

The description keeps his place in the lineage clear.

title: Īśvara Purī
summary: The renounced guru who initiates Caitanya and carries the lineage forward.
body:
Īśvara Purī is the renounced guru who initiates Caitanya. He carries the earlier line into Navadvīpa and stands immediately before Mahāprabhu in the succession followed by the Vraja temples.

This entry records that handover of the lineage.

title: Sanātana Gosvāmī
summary: A Gosvāmī instructed by Caitanya in Vārāṇasī and linked with the Madana-mohana deity.
body:
Sanātana Gosvāmī receives personal instruction from Caitanya in Vārāṇasī and later serves the Madana-mohana deity in Vraja. His work helps turn the Gauḍīya mood into a disciplined path of study and practice.

This entry notes both the instruction and the deity associated with him.

title: Rūpa Gosvāmī
summary: A Gosvāmī who shaped Gauḍīya theology and served the Govindadeva deity in Vraja.
body:
Rūpa Gosvāmī gives up courtly life to serve Kṛṣṇa in Vraja. He is closely linked with Govindadeva and becomes one of the principal theologians of the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava path.

The description preserves the change from royal service to renunciation.

title: Gadādhara Paṇḍita
summary: A learned associate and disciple of Caitanya, honoured as a teacher in the Gaura circle.
body:
Gadādhara Paṇḍita is a learned associate and disciple of Caitanya in Navadvīpa. He is honoured as a teacher in the Gaura circle and is connected with the line that reaches Mādhupandita Gosvāmī.

This entry keeps both roles visible.

title: Mādhupandita Gosvāmī
summary: The Gosvāmī linked with the Gopīnātha deity and with Gadādhara Paṇḍita's line.
body:
Mādhupandita Gosvāmī is linked with the Gopīnātha deity in Vṛndāvana and with the line of Gadādhara Paṇḍita. His name marks one of the early points where the Navadvīpa circle and Vraja service meet.

The entry records that connection.

title: Jīva Gosvāmī
summary: The theologian who organized Gauḍīya thought and cared for the Rādhā-Dāmodara deity.
body:
Jīva Gosvāmī organises Gauḍīya theology into a careful and lasting system. He cares for the Rādhā-Dāmodara deity and stands at the end of the line that runs from Rūpa Gosvāmī through Caitanya's earliest associates.

This description keeps the theologian and the deity site together.

title: Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī
summary: The elderly Gosvāmī who wrote the life of Caitanya while living at Rādhā-Dāmodara.
body:
Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja writes the life of Caitanya in his later years at Rādhā-Dāmodara. Guided by Raghunātha Dāsa and inspired by Svarūpa Dāmodara, he presents the theology of Rūpa and his circle in a form that later readers could follow.

This entry records both the place of writing and the lineage behind it.

title: Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī
summary: A renounced Gosvāmī who guided Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja and stands in the line of Caitanya's associates.
body:
Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī renounces wealth and royal ties to live in Vraja. He becomes the guru of Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja and a link between Caitanya's direct associates and later Gauḍīya writing.

The description keeps that bridge between generations in view.

title: Svarūpa Dāmodara
summary: Caitanya's intimate companion whose presence shaped Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja's writing.
body:
Svarūpa Dāmodara is Caitanya's intimate companion in Jagannātha Purī. His presence shaped the mood in which Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja later wrote, and his name marks a point where personal association becomes teaching.

This entry preserves that quiet but important link.

title: Jayadeva
summary: A poet from an earlier age whose songs on Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa were cherished by Caitanya; no initiation link is claimed.
body:
Jayadeva lived centuries before Caitanya and was not part of the Gauḍīya paramparā. His songs on Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa were nevertheless cherished in Jagannātha Purī and helped shape the rāgānugā mood later embraced in Vraja.

The entry keeps the chronological distinction clear: no initiation link is claimed.

relations.role: Relished Gīta Govinda in Jagannātha Purī; no dīkṣā link

title: Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī
summary: A renounced companion of Lokanātha who helped locate and restore sacred sites in Vraja.
body:
Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī is a renounced companion of Lokanātha Gosvāmī. Together they are remembered for finding and re-establishing sacred sites in Vraja, giving later devotees places to visit and remember.

This entry records his role as a discoverer of bhajana sites.

title: Lokanātha Gosvāmī
summary: The Gosvāmī linked with Rādhā-Gokulānanda and the teacher of Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura.
body:
Lokanātha Gosvāmī is linked with Rādhā-Gokulānanda and with the training of Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura. His life joins the discovery of Vraja's sites with the passing on of devotion to the next generation.

The description keeps both connections together.

title: Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī
summary: The Gosvāmī associated with the self-manifested Rādhā-Ramaṇa deity.
body:
Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī is associated with the self-manifested Rādhā-Ramaṇa deity in Vṛndāvana. He is remembered for careful service and for a line of teaching that continued through his disciples.

This entry marks the deity and the teacher together.

title: Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī
summary: A respected teacher traditionally accepted as Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī's initiation guru.
body:
Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī is respected as a teacher in the line connected with Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī. The relationship is traditionally accepted and is preserved here exactly as a matter of lineage.

The entry keeps the qualification visible for later review.

title: Śyāmānanda Prabhu
summary: The Gosvāmī connected with the Rādhā-Śyāmasundara deity and the line of Hṛdaya Caitanya.
body:
Śyāmānanda Prabhu is connected with the Rādhā-Śyāmasundara deity and with the line that runs through Hṛdaya Caitanya and Gauridāsa Paṇḍita. His name marks a meeting of Vraja service and Navadvīpa inheritance.

This description gathers those links.

title: Hṛdaya Caitanya
summary: The teacher who stands before Śyāmānanda Prabhu in the Rādhā-Śyāmasundara lineage.
body:
Hṛdaya Caitanya stands before Śyāmānanda Prabhu in the Rādhā-Śyāmasundara line. He is remembered as the teacher who carried the mood of devotion into that branch of Vraja service.

The entry preserves his place in the succession.

title: Gauridāsa Paṇḍita
summary: A teacher in that same line, linked through a guru who directly knew Caitanya.
body:
Gauridāsa Paṇḍita is a teacher in the same line, linked through a guru who directly knew Caitanya. His name keeps the Navadvīpa origin of that branch visible beside its later Vraja deity.

This entry records the human link behind the lineage.

title: Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura
summary: A devoted disciple of Lokanātha Gosvāmī who carried the Vraja tradition forward.
body:
Narottama Dāsa Ṭhākura is a devoted disciple of Lokanātha Gosvāmī. He carries forward the Vraja tradition of deity service, sacred sites and singing that his guru helped establish.

The description keeps teacher and disciple together.

title: Vajranābha
summary: The figure credited in tradition with setting up sixteen principal deities throughout Vraja Maṇḍala.
body:
Vajranābha is credited in tradition with setting up sixteen principal deities across Vraja Maṇḍala. His name therefore appears wherever those sites are gathered, as the figure who gave them a shared sacred map.

This entry preserves that organizing role.
